The secondary-stressed first syllable splits: MedlinePlus's Aripiprazole monograph and AHD have 'ay'; MedlinePlus's newer Aripiprazole Injection monograph ('ar″ I pip′ ra zole'), Merriam-Webster and Wiktionary GA have the 'a' of 'arrow'. With MedlinePlus split against itself, the dictionaries decide (two of three for 'a'), as the guide does when monographs disagree. Medium because the sources split on that stressed vowel; 'ay' is the alternative. The fourth syllable is reduced (the -prazole family; the injection monograph and every dictionary write 'ra'/'rə'; d0001 omeprazole).
